response: Biodegradable waste (food scraps, peels, garden waste) goes in the Green Bin. It decomposes naturally and can be composted at home in 30-60 days. Keep it separate from plastic so your compost stays clean.

Recyclable dry waste (clean plastic, paper, glass, metal) goes in the Blue Bin. Rinse containers first and flatten cardboard - contamination with food waste is the biggest reason recyclables get rejected.
Non-recyclable/reject waste (soiled multi-layer wrappers, broken ceramics, cigarette butts) goes in the Black Bin for landfill/waste-to-energy. Never burn this waste - it releases toxic fumes.

E-waste (phones, laptops, chargers, batteries, TVs) should NEVER go in regular bins - it contains lead, mercury and cadmium. Wipe your data, then hand it to an authorised e-waste collection point or a manufacturer take-back programme.

Hazardous waste (paints, chemicals, expired medicines, CFL bulbs, syringes) needs specialised handling. Never pour it down the drain or mix with regular waste - return it to a pharmacy take-back scheme or a hazardous-waste facility.

This project uses a YOLOv8 object-detection model to spot multiple items in a live webcam feed or an uploaded photo, then a rule-based classification engine maps each detected object to a waste category (biodegradable, recyclable, non-recyclable, e-waste or hazardous) with disposal guidance - all running locally, no cloud required.

Every correctly segregated item earns eco-points (5-20 depending on category) shown on your Dashboard. Rack up points to level up your badge from Rookie Sorter all the way to Platinum Segregator, and keep a daily streak going by scanning waste every day!
